userStories.title: nax-agent: backend ask/deny rules and sandbox config
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add optional rule overlays and configured sandbox input to native sessions without changing existing profiles.

**Motivation** — Testing v0.91.7-canary.3 showed that in guarded mode every command (the repo's own typecheck included) and every edit waited for approval.

**Approach** — `NativeBackendOptions` gains `askRules`, `denyRules` and `sandbox`. A new `nativePostureRules` (new file `native-posture-rules.ts`) parses the rule lists with `parseRuleList` and parses `sandbox`; `openNative` adds the rules after the profile's own and hands the parsed sandbox config to `resolveSessionLauncher`, which falls back to `DEFAULT_SANDBOX_CONFIG` when absent. Tool-only askRules and denyRules are refused on none/read.

Verbatim design targets for this slice:
- `NativeBackendOptions` / `OptionsSchema`: adds `askRules?: readonly string[]`, `denyRules?: readonly string[]` (each entry a non-empty string), `sandbox?: z.input<typeof SandboxConfigSchema>` (the schema's INPUT type, so a partial object is accepted; validated by `SandboxConfigSchema` inside `OptionsSchema`).
- `nativePostureRules(profile: AgentSessionProfile, raw: NativeBackendOptions): ResolvedPostureRules`: US-001 creates the function with `askRules`, `denyRules` and `sandbox` (and the `askRules`/`denyRules`/`sandbox` option fields); US-002 adds `askOnUnsandboxed`, `askWhenSandboxDown`, `askDiscoveredTools`, `effectiveBashApproval` and the matching option fields. `sandbox` is the parsed `SandboxConfigSchema` value, `DEFAULT_SANDBOX_CONFIG` when absent.
- `SessionLauncherArgs` adds `readonly config?: SandboxConfig`; the launcher resolves with `args.config ?? DEFAULT_SANDBOX_CONFIG`.
- `SessionToolSupportArgs` adds `askRules?: readonly ToolGrant[]`, `denyRules?: readonly ToolGrant[]` (US-001); the ask rules passed down are `askRulesFor(...)`, then the provider ask tools (when `profile === "ask"` in this slice), then `args.askRules`. `denyRules` are forwarded when present.

`askRules` and `denyRules` are parsed with `parseRuleList` and appended after the profile's ask rules and the provider ask tools; `denyRules` likewise become `denyRules`. `parseRuleList(expressions: readonly string[]): ToolGrant[]` is exported from `@nathapp/nax-agent` (never throws). Preserve deny-before-ask behavior and the unconditional Bash deny under raw; do not modify the raw Bash branch. Backend option failures throw AgentSessionError code AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_OPTIONS naming backend.askRules, backend.denyRules or backend.sandbox. Tool-less profile failures identify backend.<name>.

Complexity (the nax-agent complexity gate is 20 per function and `buildCodingToolSupport` is baselined and may not grow): the new option checks live in a new `nativePostureRules` function in a new file `packages/nax-agent/src/session/native-posture-rules.ts`, written as a loop over a table of tool-only option names rather than one `if` per option. `openNative` already scores 19 against the limit of 20, so it passes every new value to `buildSessionToolSupport` as a plain property (the way it passes `interceptor: raw.hostPorts?.commandInterceptor`), never as a new conditional spread; `buildSessionToolSupport` forwards its new fields through one helper rather than one spread each. The same helper will be extended in US-002. OptionsSchema preserves raw identity, so posture resolution must separately produce parsed/default-filled sandbox output. Extend the existing shared agent-session.ts test factory's native-option forwarding if using it for the new session tests.

**Scope** — In: native-backend-options.ts, new native-posture-rules.ts, native-backend.ts, session-tool-support.ts, shared test factory forwarding if used, new posture tests and existing options/support tests. Out: escape/sandbox-down/discovered-tool flags and commandShadow port (US-002), tui config resolution (US-003), chat wiring (US-004), shadow lifecycle/instructions (US-005). The nax-agent `ask` profile, `askRulesFor`, `nativeProfileRules` and its return shape keep their behaviour; no embedder's options change meaning. Every new option is optional and absent keeps today's behaviour; existing nativeProfileRules toEqual assertions retain their shapes.

**Interface** — `nativePostureRules(profile: AgentSessionProfile, raw: NativeBackendOptions): ResolvedPostureRules`. This slice's result is `interface ResolvedPostureRules { readonly askRules: readonly ToolGrant[]; readonly denyRules: readonly ToolGrant[]; readonly sandbox: SandboxConfig }`; US-002 extends it with booleans. `NativeBackendOptions` gains `askRules?: readonly string[]`, `denyRules?: readonly string[]`, `sandbox?: z.input<typeof SandboxConfigSchema>`. `SessionLauncherArgs` gains `readonly config?: SandboxConfig`; `SessionToolSupportArgs` gains `askRules?: readonly ToolGrant[]`, `denyRules?: readonly ToolGrant[]`.

Test placement: session-level integration ACs in a new `packages/nax-agent/test/unit/session/native-backend-posture.test.ts`; `nativePostureRules` ACs in a new `packages/nax-agent/test/unit/session/native-posture-rules.test.ts`; `parseNativeBackendOptions` ACs in the existing `native-backend-options.test.ts`; `buildSessionToolSupport` and `resolveSessionLauncher` ACs in the existing `session-tool-support.test.ts`. Use stubSessionSandboxDeps and the existing scripted provider/ask harness, prove regressions fail against old code, then implement without altering test-writer assertions.

[unit] parseNativeBackendOptions rejects each askRules or denyRules value that is not an array of non-empty strings with AgentSessionError code AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_OPTIONS and a message naming backend.askRules or backend.denyRules respectively.

[unit] When sandbox input fails SandboxConfigSchema, parseNativeBackendOptions throws AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_OPTIONS with a reported path starting backend.sandbox.

routing.reasoning: New posture resolver integrates validated public backend options, sandbox resolution and tool-policy precedence across session modules; access-control/session changes require strict three-session isolation.

userStories.title: nax-agent: escape, sandbox-down and discovered-tool asks, command shadow port
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add opt-in asks for sandbox escape, missing sandbox and discovered mutating tools, plus a command-shadow host port.

**Motivation** — The slice-1 design intended "guarded = the existing guard decides".

**Approach** — `NativeBackendOptions` gains `askOnUnsandboxed`, `askWhenSandboxDown`, `askDiscoveredTools` and `hostPorts.commandShadow`, validated by the backend option schema and `nativePostureRules` as appropriate. An escape request asks even under `raw` when `askOnUnsandboxed` is set; a sandbox that did not resolve `available` makes every Bash ask when `askWhenSandboxDown` is set; `askDiscoveredTools` keeps the non-read-only MCP asks under profile `full`; the command shadow reaches the tool runtime so its guard can flag commands.

Verbatim mechanism design:
- Unsandboxed escape (`unsandboxed: true` on Bash): `askOnUnsandboxed: true` sets `alwaysAsk` on the runtime's `unsandboxed` option; `resolveUnsandboxedCall` returns `asksOnAllow: true` even under `raw`, and `convertUnsandboxedAllow` turns the allowed verdict into an ask whose `reason` carries the escape reason.
- Sandbox unavailable or disabled: `askWhenSandboxDown: true`: when `resolveSessionLauncher` reports a sandbox state whose `kind` is not `"available"`, `openNative` builds the tool support, and the adapter's `resolvedPermissions`, with `bashApproval: "gated"`, so `askRulesFor` adds the `Bash(*)` ask.
- commandSafety guard: `hostPorts.commandShadow` reaches `buildCodingToolSupport`'s `commandShadow`; the runtime's existing guard (`resolveGuardDenial`) turns a flagged allowed `Bash`/`Exec` call into an ask.
- Non-read-only discovered MCP tool: `askDiscoveredTools: true` makes `buildSessionToolSupport` add `providerTools.askTools` under profile `full`, as it already does under `ask`.

Verbatim option/forwarding targets: adds `askOnUnsandboxed?: boolean`, `askWhenSandboxDown?: boolean`, `askDiscoveredTools?: boolean`; `hostPorts` adds `commandShadow?: CommandShadow` (validated as an object with `observe`, `settle` and `drain` methods). Each of the five options is refused on profiles `none` and `read` with `AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_OPTIONS` naming the option's path (`backend.<name>`); `askOnUnsandboxed: true` without `allowUnsandboxedCommands: true` is refused. The five tool-only names are askRules, denyRules, askOnUnsandboxed, askWhenSandboxDown and askDiscoveredTools. `effectiveBashApproval(profileMode, askWhenSandboxDown, sandboxKind)` returns `"gated"` when `askWhenSandboxDown` is true and `sandboxKind` is not `"available"`, else `profileMode`.

`SessionToolSupportArgs` adds `askOnUnsandboxed?: boolean`, `askDiscoveredTools?: boolean`, `commandShadow?: CommandShadow`; the ask rules passed down are `askRulesFor(...)`, then the provider ask tools (when `profile === "ask"` or `askDiscoveredTools`), then `args.askRules`; `denyRules`, `askOnUnsandboxed` and `commandShadow` are forwarded when present. `unsandboxedRuntimeOption(args)` takes `askOnUnsandboxed?: boolean`; returns `{ unsandboxed: { enabled: true, bashApproval, alwaysAsk: true } }` when both are true, and the baseline shape (no `alwaysAsk` key) otherwise. `resolveUnsandboxedCall`'s option becomes `{ readonly enabled: boolean; readonly bashApproval: BashApprovalMode; readonly alwaysAsk?: boolean }`; `asksOnAllow` is `option.alwaysAsk === true || option.bashApproval !== "raw"`. `buildCodingToolSupport` args adds `askOnUnsandboxed?: boolean`, forwarded as a plain property into `unsandboxedRuntimeOption`. `openNative` takes the effective mode from `effectiveBashApproval`; passes the effective mode, rule lists, `askOnUnsandboxed`, `askDiscoveredTools` and `raw.hostPorts?.commandShadow` to `buildSessionToolSupport`, and the effective mode to `openSession`'s `resolvedPermissions`.

Complexity (the nax-agent complexity gate is 20 per function and `buildCodingToolSupport` is baselined and may not grow): the new option checks live in a new `nativePostureRules` function in a new file `packages/nax-agent/src/session/native-posture-rules.ts`, written as a loop over a table of tool-only option names rather than one `if` per option; `openNative` takes the effective mode from `effectiveBashApproval(profileMode, askWhenSandboxDown, sandboxKind)` in the same file; `askOnUnsandboxed` reaches `unsandboxedRuntimeOption` as a plain property, with no new ternary inside `buildCodingToolSupport`. `openNative` already scores 19 against the limit of 20, so it passes every new value to `buildSessionToolSupport` as a plain property (the way it passes `interceptor: raw.hostPorts?.commandInterceptor`), never as a new conditional spread; `buildSessionToolSupport` forwards its new fields through one helper rather than one spread each. `packages/nax-agent/src/tools/runtime.ts` is exactly at its 600-line limit: the widened `unsandboxed` option type stays on its existing single line, with no new line, comment or import.

**Scope** — In: extend US-001 posture resolver and backend schema, AgentSessionHostPorts, session support, coding-tool extras/support, runtime option and escape routing, native adapter effective permissions, new asks tests. Out: tui resolver (US-003), chat/subagent posture wiring (US-004), main chat shadow construction/draining and prompt text (US-005). The sandbox state is decided once when a session opens; a sandbox that becomes unavailable mid-session does not switch that session to asking until it is reopened (resume, `/mode` or `/model` switch). The nax-agent `ask` profile, `askRulesFor`, `nativeProfileRules` and its return shape keep their behaviour; no embedder's options change meaning. `alwaysAsk` is added only when `askOnUnsandboxed` is true, and provider ask tools under profile `full` are added only when `askDiscoveredTools` is true, so every existing `unsandboxedRuntimeOption`, `resolveUnsandboxedCall` and `buildSessionToolSupport` expectation keeps its shape.

**Interface** — `nativePostureRules(profile: AgentSessionProfile, raw: NativeBackendOptions): ResolvedPostureRules` with `interface ResolvedPostureRules { readonly askRules: readonly ToolGrant[]; readonly denyRules: readonly ToolGrant[]; readonly sandbox: SandboxConfig; readonly askOnUnsandboxed: boolean; readonly askWhenSandboxDown: boolean; readonly askDiscoveredTools: boolean }`. `effectiveBashApproval(profileMode, askWhenSandboxDown, sandboxKind)` is in native-posture-rules.ts. `AgentSessionHostPorts` adds `readonly commandShadow?: CommandShadow`. `CommandShadow { observe, settle, drain, guard? }` is the existing type, not a new implementation.

Test placement: session-level integration ACs in a new `packages/nax-agent/test/unit/session/native-backend-asks.test.ts`; `nativePostureRules` and `effectiveBashApproval` ACs in `native-posture-rules.test.ts` (created by US-001); `unsandboxedRuntimeOption` ACs in the existing `test/unit/coding-tools/coding-tool-extras.test.ts`; `resolveUnsandboxedCall` ACs in the existing `test/unit/tools/runtime-unsandboxed.test.ts`; `buildSessionToolSupport` and `parseNativeBackendOptions` ACs in their existing test files. Stub sandbox availability explicitly; extend native-option forwarding in the shared session test factory if used. Demonstrate old-code failure before implementation.

[integration] When askWhenSandboxDown turns the mode to gated, the native adapter's openSession receives resolvedPermissions.bashApproval equal to "gated".

[unit] buildSessionToolSupport called with profile full, askDiscoveredTools: true and provider tools whose askTools is ["docs__write"] hands buildCodingToolSupport ask rules containing { tool: "docs__write", patterns: ["*"] }.

[integration] A session opened with profile full, bashApproval: "raw" and hostPorts.commandShadow set to a fake shadow whose guard.assess flags every command puts a Bash call to the ask port.

[unit] nativePostureRules rejects askOnUnsandboxed, askWhenSandboxDown and askDiscoveredTools when any is set on either profile none or read with AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_OPTIONS naming backend.<option>.

routing.reasoning: Cross-module permission overlays span escape routing, sandbox fallback, provider asks and a host guard port with strict compatibility and complexity constraints; sessions/access-control require strict TDD isolation.

userStories.title: nax: resolve the tui permission posture
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve guarded chat's tui bash mode and ask/deny lists from existing execution configuration.

**Motivation** — The user's global config runs `nax run` with `bashApproval: "raw"` inside the sandbox, without asking.

**Approach** — `resolveTuiPermissions(config)` in `src/config/permissions.ts` walks `execution.permissions.tui` -> its `inherit` chain -> `default`, resolves `bashApproval` against the top-level value, maps `escalate` to `gated` with one warning, and returns the block's `ask` and `deny` lists verbatim. Exported from `@/config`.

Verbatim design targets:
- `lookupStageBlock` takes `stage: string` (file-local); new export `resolveTuiPermissions(config: AgentManagerConfig | undefined): TuiPermissions` with `interface TuiPermissions { readonly bashApproval: "raw" | "gated"; readonly askRules: readonly string[]; readonly denyRules: readonly string[] }`, both exported from `@/config`. `stageRules` and `resolvePermissions` are unchanged; `resolveTuiPermissions` reads the looked-up block's `ask`, `deny` and `bashApproval` directly.
- `resolveBashApproval(global, perStage): BashApprovalMode` — `packages/nax-agent/src/config/bash-approval.ts`, re-exported from `@nathapp/nax-agent/internal`.
- `validatePermissionsBlock` (`packages/nax/src/config/config-guards.ts`) already accepts any block key, and `PermissionsBlockSchema` is `z.record(z.string(), ...)`, so `execution.permissions.tui` loads without a schema change.

Resolved `bashApproval` semantics for guarded, matching `nax run` (ADR-030):
- `raw`: commands inside the sandbox run without asking. Under `raw` the Bash branch does not consult pattern-scoped `Bash(...)` ask or deny rules (`commandBranch` in `packages/nax-agent/src/tools/policy-command-branch.ts` returns before `askBy`/`denyBy`); an unconditional `Bash` / `Bash(*)` deny is still honoured, because `compileToolPolicy` checks it before the command branch. This is existing `nax run` behaviour and is kept. Ask and deny rules for every other tool (`Write`, `Edit`, `Delete`, `Git`) apply under every mode.
- `gated`: every Bash command asks (the existing `askRulesFor` `Bash(*)` ask).
- `escalate`: has no meaning in chat (chat grants `Bash(*)`, so no grant miss exists to escalate, and `nativeProfileRules` refuses `escalate` with `allowUnsandboxed`). It resolves to `gated` and `resolveTuiPermissions` logs one warning.

Failure warning text is exact: when resolved raw has pattern-scoped Bash ask/deny rules, log one warn on stage `"permissions"` with message `[tui] Bash(...) ask/deny patterns are not consulted under bashApproval "raw"`; keep the configured lists unchanged. When resolved escalate, log one warn on stage `"permissions"` with message `[tui] bashApproval "escalate" has no meaning in chat; using "gated"`. Use getSafeLogger and the existing whole-block lookup, not new merging or pipeline policy resolution. Undefined config resolves to raw and empty lists.

**Scope** — In: permissions.ts new resolver/interface, file-local lookup argument widening, config/index.ts named exports, unit and loader integration assertions. Out: nax-agent backend options (US-001/002), chat session callers (US-004), shadow lifecycle/instructions (US-005). `allow` and legacy `allowedTools` lists in `execution.permissions.tui` are not read: chat's `full` profile already grants every tool, so an allow list cannot widen anything. A `tui` block replaces the `default` block as a whole (existing block-lookup semantics): a `tui` block that sets only `bashApproval` does not inherit `default`'s `ask` or `deny` lists unless it names `inherit: "default"`. `execution.permissionProfile` is not read by chat. `Mcp(...)` rules are not expanded here. Do not add tui to PipelineStage or modify stageRules/resolvePermissions.

**Interface** — `resolveTuiPermissions(config: AgentManagerConfig | undefined): TuiPermissions`; `interface TuiPermissions { readonly bashApproval: "raw" | "gated"; readonly askRules: readonly string[]; readonly denyRules: readonly string[] }`; `lookupStageBlock` takes `stage: string` (file-local).

Extend packages/nax/test/unit/config/permissions.test.ts and existing config-loader integration coverage. Capture warn count, stage and exact messages using existing logger/test seams, prove old-code failure, and preserve every pipeline permission assertion.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] resolveTuiPermissions(config) with no execution.permissions and execution.bashApproval: "raw" returns exactly { bashApproval: "raw", askRules: [], denyRules: [] }.
[unit] With no execution.permissions and execution.bashApproval: "gated", resolveTuiPermissions returns bashApproval: "gated".
[unit] With execution.bashApproval: "raw" and execution.permissions.tui.bashApproval: "gated", resolveTuiPermissions returns bashApproval: "gated".
[unit] With no tui block and execution.permissions.default.bashApproval: "gated", resolveTuiPermissions returns bashApproval: "gated".
[unit] With execution.permissions.tui.ask: ["Write"] and execution.permissions.default.ask: ["Delete"], resolveTuiPermissions returns askRules equal to ["Write"] (the tui block wins over default).
[unit] With execution.permissions.tui: { inherit: "run" } and execution.permissions.run.deny: ["Delete(src/**)"], resolveTuiPermissions returns denyRules equal to ["Delete(src/**)"].
[unit] With execution.permissions.tui.ask: ["Bash(git push*)", "Write(docs/**)"], resolveTuiPermissions returns askRules equal to ["Bash(git push*)", "Write(docs/**)"], in order.
[unit] With execution.permissions.tui.bashApproval: "escalate", resolveTuiPermissions returns bashApproval: "gated".
[unit] With top-level execution.bashApproval: "escalate" and no execution.permissions, resolveTuiPermissions returns bashApproval: "gated".

[unit] With execution.bashApproval: "raw" and execution.permissions.tui.ask: ["Bash(git push*)"], resolveTuiPermissions logs exactly one warn on stage "permissions" whose message contains not consulted.
[unit] With execution.bashApproval: "raw" and execution.permissions.tui.ask: ["Write"], resolveTuiPermissions logs no warn.
[unit] Resolving the tui-block escalate config logs exactly one warn on stage "permissions" whose message contains escalate and tui.
[unit] With execution.permissions.tui.allow: ["Bash(ls*)"], resolveTuiPermissions result's keys are exactly bashApproval, askRules and denyRules.
[unit] resolveTuiPermissions(undefined) returns { bashApproval: "raw", askRules: [], denyRules: [] }.
[unit] resolveTuiPermissions is importable from @/config and is a function.

[unit] With an execution.permissions.tui block carrying bashApproval: "gated" and ask: ["Write"], resolvePermissions(config, "run") returns bashApproval equal to the top-level value and no askRules (the tui block never leaks into a pipeline stage).

[integration] Loading a project config whose execution.permissions.tui is { "bashApproval": "gated", "ask": ["Write"], "deny": ["Delete(src/**)"] } through the config loader succeeds, and resolveTuiPermissions on the loaded config returns that bashApproval, askRules and denyRules.

[unit] When resolved bashApproval is raw and either selected ask or deny list contains pattern-scoped Bash(...) rules, resolveTuiPermissions logs exactly one warn on stage "permissions" with message `[tui] Bash(...) ask/deny patterns are not consulted under bashApproval "raw"`.
[unit] When resolved bashApproval is raw and either selected ask or deny list contains pattern-scoped Bash(...) rules, resolveTuiPermissions returns those configured rule lists unchanged.

[unit] When selected or top-level bashApproval resolves to escalate, resolveTuiPermissions logs exactly one warn on stage "permissions" with message `[tui] bashApproval "escalate" has no meaning in chat; using "gated"`.

routing.reasoning: Reuses established block lookup and approval resolver with a small additive config API, but permission resolution is access control and requires the security override.

suggestedCriteria: With a tui block containing only bashApproval: "gated" and default.ask: ["Delete"], resolveTuiPermissions returns askRules: [] rather than inheriting default.ask.
With execution.bashApproval: "raw" and tui.deny: ["Bash(*)"], resolveTuiPermissions logs no ignored-pattern warning.

userStories.title: nax: guarded chat and subagent sessions open with the resolved posture
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Open guarded main and subagent sessions using the full native profile and one current-config posture resolution per open.

**Motivation** — `chatSessionSettings("guarded")` (`packages/nax/src/chat/chat-mode.ts`) hard-codes the nax-agent `ask` profile with `bashApproval: "gated"`.

**Approach** — `chatSessionSettings` takes the posture and opens the `full` profile in both modes; `chatBackendPosture` builds the extra backend options; `openChatSession` and `runSubagent` each resolve the posture once per open and pass it to `nativeBackend`; `openChatSession` records the resolved `bashApproval` in the metadata.

Verbatim design targets:
- `chatSessionSettings(mode: ChatMode, posture: TuiPermissions | undefined): ChatSessionSettings` with `profile: "full"` in both modes; guarded -> `{ profile: "full", bashApproval: posture.bashApproval, metaMode: "ask" }`; full -> `{ profile: "full", bashApproval: "raw", metaMode: "full" }` (posture ignored); guarded with an undefined posture throws `NaxError` code `CHAT_POSTURE_REQUIRED` (a wiring error, never a user path). The posture is resolved ONLY for guarded opens, so a full open never logs a posture warning.
- New export `chatBackendPosture(mode: ChatMode, config: NaxConfig, posture: TuiPermissions | undefined)` (also exported from `packages/nax/src/chat/index.ts`) returning the extra `nativeBackend` options: in both modes `sandbox: config.execution.sandbox`; in guarded additionally `askRules: posture.askRules`, `denyRules: posture.denyRules`, `askOnUnsandboxed: true`, `askWhenSandboxDown: true`, `askDiscoveredTools: true`.
- `_openChatSessionDeps`, `sessionMeta`, `sessionOptions`, `openChatSession`: deps gain `resolveTuiPermissions`; for a guarded open the posture is resolved once from `request.config`, and that single value is passed to both `sessionMeta` and `sessionOptions` (and so to `chatSessionSettings` and `chatBackendPosture`); a full open resolves none.
- `_subagentSessionDeps`, `subagentSessionOptions`: deps gain `resolveTuiPermissions` (called only in guarded mode); the subagent's options use `chatSessionSettings(input.mode, posture)` and spread `chatBackendPosture(input.mode, input.config, posture)` into `nativeBackend`.

Session metadata: a guarded session keeps `SessionMeta.mode: "ask"` (so `chatModeOfMeta` still identifies it as guarded) and records the resolved `bashApproval`. Resume and mode switches recompute the posture from the current config; the stored `bashApproval` is never read back as policy. Permission resolution site: `adapter-wiring.md` rule 5 says permissions resolve at the resource opener. `openChatSession` and `runSubagent` ARE chat's resource openers (each opens exactly one native session), so `resolveTuiPermissions` is called there once per open, never deeper. Determine effective resume mode from validated stored mode plus any explicit mode switch before choosing whether to resolve; preserve stored-mode validation before lock ownership. Do not resolve again in sessionMeta/sessionOptions/subagentSessionOptions.

The chat sandbox (both modes) is built from `execution.sandbox`. Existing allowUnsandboxed: true and allowUnsandboxedCommands: true remain; therefore a guarded open with sandbox unavailable or disabled still opens and every Bash command asks via US-002's effective gated mode. Preserve tool providers, narrowing, compaction, model history, loop handler roles and approval timeout. Native profile full does not replace guarded metadata ask.

**Scope** — In: chat-mode.ts/settings/helper, chat/index.ts export, opener deps and dataflow, metadata in-memory recomputation, subagent deps and options, corresponding expectation updates. Out: agent posture implementation (US-001/002), config resolver implementation (US-003), command-shadow construction/draining and instruction sentence (US-005). Full mode does not read `execution.permissions.tui` or `execution.commandSafety` and never asks; its only change is that its sandbox is built from `execution.sandbox`. Subagent sessions do not receive a command shadow or the commandSafety guard; the subagent's own posture (bash mode, ask/deny rules, escape, sandbox-down and discovered-tool asks, sandbox config) is wired. No migration of stored session metadata: a stored `bashApproval` is overwritten in memory at open and written only where it is written today. No TUI footer, picker or mode-behavior changes.

**Interface** — `chatSessionSettings(mode: ChatMode, posture: TuiPermissions | undefined): ChatSessionSettings`; `chatBackendPosture(mode: ChatMode, config: NaxConfig, posture: TuiPermissions | undefined)`. `ChatSessionSettings` has `profile: "full"`, `bashApproval: "raw" | "gated"`, `metaMode: "full" | "ask"`. Consume `resolveTuiPermissions(config: AgentManagerConfig | undefined): TuiPermissions` only at each resource opener.

Existing test modifications are binding: chat-mode.test.ts passes posture { bashApproval: "raw", askRules: [], denyRules: [] } and changes guarded settings from ask/gated to full/raw, leaving full/nextChatMode/chatModeOfMeta expectations unchanged. open-chat-session.test.ts AC-1, AC-11 and explicit-switch guarded bashApproval become raw, while AC-2/3/4, mode ask and stored metadata assertions remain unchanged. chat-host-resume.test.ts profile-recorded orders become ["open:full", "close", "open:full"] and ["open:full", "close", "open:full", "open:full"]; AC-13 optionsSeen[2] expects profile full, preserving host mode, metadata and locks. subagent-session.test.ts typed deps setup gains resolveTuiPermissions: mock(() => ({ bashApproval: "raw", askRules: [], denyRules: [] })); guarded AC-1 profile becomes full and AC-3 bashApproval becomes raw, full AC-2/4 unchanged. host-subagents.test.ts AC-8 title and nested profile expectation change ask to full/["full"], rest unchanged. Add seam tests for one resolver call per guarded open, zero in full, backend posture identity/values, both sandbox modes and resume policy recomputation; show old-code failure first.

userStories.title: nax: command shadow in guarded chat and guarded instruction text
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Wire configured command safety into guarded main chat with reliable shadow cleanup and update the shared guarded permission sentence.

**Motivation** — The chat session never reads `execution.bashApproval`, `execution.permissions` or `execution.commandSafety`, and `resolveSessionLauncher` always uses `DEFAULT_SANDBOX_CONFIG`, so `execution.sandbox` (for example `network.allowedDomains` for package registries) never reaches chat either.

**Approach** — `openChatSession` builds the command shadow for guarded sessions, hands it to the backend, and drains it on release and on a failed open. The guarded permission paragraph shared by the chat and subagent instructions describes the new asks.

Verbatim design targets:
- The commandSafety shadow and guard (`execution.commandSafety`) are wired into the guarded main session through the existing `buildCommandShadow`.
- `_openChatSessionDeps`, `sessionMeta`, `sessionOptions`, `openChatSession`: deps gain `buildCommandShadow`; guarded builds the shadow (`outputDir: request.storage.dir`, `runId: meta.sessionId`, `env: deps.env`) and passes it as `hostPorts.commandShadow`; the returned `release` drains the shadow, then releases the lock.
- `buildCommandShadow({ config, outputDir, runId, storyId?, env }): CommandShadow | undefined` — `packages/nax-agent/src/command-safety/build.ts`, exported from `@nathapp/nax-agent`; returns `undefined` when `config?.shadow` is absent.
- `CommandShadow { observe, settle, drain, guard? }` — `packages/nax-agent/src/command-safety/types.ts`.

Command-safety rows from chat land under the chat sessions directory (`<sessionsDir>/command-safety/<sessionId>.jsonl`), not a project output directory; the session store lists only `*.session.json`, so the rows never collide with session files.

Failure handling: `execution.commandSafety` absent, or present without `shadow`: `buildCommandShadow` returns `undefined`; the backend gets no `hostPorts` key and nothing is drained. The session open fails after the shadow was built (`nativeBackend` throws, `createAgentSession`/`resumeAgentSession` rejects): the shadow is drained and the lock released before the error propagates. The shadow's classifier is unreachable: Existing `buildCommandShadow` behaviour (bounded by its own timeout; the guard never rejects); nothing new. Preserve the same original error on failed opens, and record drain before lock release. Full opens never call buildCommandShadow. Use the existing builder and runtime port rather than the broader run dispatch-ask wiring, approvals store or a separate guard implementation.

**Scope** — In: main opener deps, build/forward/drain lifetime, failed-open cleanup, shared chatPermissionParagraph and corresponding chat/subagent instruction assertions. Out: backend/runtime implementation (US-001/002), config resolver (US-003), session mode/posture wiring (US-004). Subagent sessions do not receive a command shadow or the commandSafety guard; the subagent's own posture (bash mode, ask/deny rules, escape, sandbox-down and discovered-tool asks, sandbox config) is wired. Full mode does not read `execution.permissions.tui` or `execution.commandSafety` and never asks; its only change is that its sandbox is built from `execution.sandbox`. No TUI wording changes besides the instruction paragraph: the footer label, the `/mode` picker text (`asks before risky actions`) and `/mode` behaviour are unchanged.

**Interface** — `_openChatSessionDeps` gains `buildCommandShadow`; `buildCommandShadow({ config, outputDir, runId, storyId?, env }): CommandShadow | undefined`; `hostPorts: { commandShadow }` is included only when a shadow exists. `chatPermissionParagraph(mode)` guarded return is exactly: `In guarded mode, commands run inside the sandbox under the configured posture; a command that asks to run outside the sandbox, any command while the sandbox is unavailable, a call the configured permission rules mark for asking, and a call to an MCP tool that is not read-only are put to the person before they run.` Do not append new prose about commandSafety to this exact sentence. Full text remains `In full mode, tools run without asking.`

Extend open-chat-session.test.ts using injected fake shadows and ordered drain/lock markers; cover nativeBackend synchronous throw, create rejection and resume rejection after building. Show new regressions fail against old code first. chat-builder.test.ts AC-3 guarded text changes to the exact new sentence, AC-4 full assertions unchanged. agents-builder.test.ts full-string expectation at the chat `## Permission mode` section replaces only the guarded sentence; the contains-guarded case's literal prefix becomes `In guarded mode, commands run inside the sandbox`, keeping its chatPermissionParagraph assertion. agents-builder already shares the sentence; do not change unrelated prompt composition.

[unit] openChatSession for a full session never calls buildCommandShadow.
[unit] Calling the returned handle.release() for a guarded session with a fake shadow calls the shadow's drain before the storage lock is released (recorded call order: drain, then the lock release).

[unit] When the injected createAgentSession rejects after the shadow was built, openChatSession rejects with that same error, after calling the shadow's drain exactly once and releasing the storage lock.
[unit] When the injected nativeBackend throws after the shadow was built, openChatSession rejects with that same error, after calling the shadow's drain exactly once and releasing the storage lock.

[unit] chatPermissionParagraph("guarded") returns exactly "In guarded mode, commands run inside the sandbox under the configured posture; a command that asks to run outside the sandbox, any command while the sandbox is unavailable, a call the configured permission rules mark for asking, and a call to an MCP tool that is not read-only are put to the person before they run."
[unit] buildChatInstructions({ mode: "guarded", rulesIndex: [] }) places that sentence in the ## Permission mode section.
[unit] buildChatInstructions({ mode: "full", rulesIndex: [] }) returns text that includes tools run without asking and omits put to the person before they run.
[unit] When execution.commandSafety is absent or present without shadow, buildCommandShadow returns undefined and openChatSession passes no hostPorts key to nativeBackend.
[unit] When buildCommandShadow returns undefined, releasing a successful guarded handle releases the storage lock without draining a shadow.
[unit] When the injected resumeAgentSession rejects after the shadow was built, openChatSession rejects with that same error after draining the shadow and releasing the storage lock.

[integration] Given a guarded main session with commandSafety.shadow and commandSafety.guard configured, when its classifier request times out as unreachable, the forwarded commandShadow.guard.assess({ command: "echo ok", cwd: request.cwd, tempConfined: false }) resolves a GuardDecision with basis: "rules" rather than rejecting (bounded by the existing classifier timeout; preserving existing buildCommandShadow behavior).

routing.reasoning: Two source changes reuse the existing shadow builder and shared prompt function; ordered cleanup extends an existing lock try/catch without a new abstraction. Session/guard access-control wiring still requires strict three-session TDD under the security override.

suggestedCriteria: When a guarded open builds a command shadow, buildCommandShadow receives env equal to _openChatSessionDeps.env.
When buildSubagentInstructions receives mode guarded, its result contains the same exact guarded sentence returned by chatPermissionParagraph.

modifiedFiles.reason: AC-3's expected guarded text changes from `edits, deletes, commits and every shell command are put to the person before they run` to the new guarded sentence in US-005; AC-4's full-mode assertions are unchanged.

the full-string expectation at the `## Permission mode` section replaces the old guarded sentence with the new guarded sentence in US-005; the "contains the guarded permission paragraph" case's literal `In guarded mode, edits, deletes, commits` becomes `In guarded mode, commands run inside the sandbox` (its `chatPermissionParagraph("guarded")` assertion is unchanged).

analysis:
Refine-pass audit: enumerated all 89 explicit spec ACs and retained their assertions and regression qualifiers in the same stories: US-001 AC1-19, US-002 AC1-22, US-003 AC1-17, US-004 AC1-21, US-005 AC1-10. Supplemental criteria cover all 11 failure-table rows; each story has a negative path and backward-compatibility assertions. All 13 feature out-of-scope items remain verbatim, with relevant boundaries echoed in descriptions. All binding ids, workdirs and dependencies are unchanged; all spec-recommended context files are included, and outputs are separated from context. Re-read the current session/config/guard/prompt implementations. Clarified the unreachable-classifier AC to an observable forwarded commandShadow.guard.assess return rather than an unspecified assessment: packages/nax-agent/src/command-safety/guard.ts:112 returns basis rules on unavailable classifier results, and packages/nax-agent/src/command-safety/guard.ts:176 makes assess total. This does not add or change a guard algorithm. Reduced US-005 complexity to medium because it reuses the existing builder, opener cleanup and shared paragraph; its security-critical test strategy remains three-session-tdd. No spec AC was removed, moved or weakened, and no feature exclusion was promoted to an AC.

Enhancement/bug fix for #2712, not greenfield. Discovery used direct reads and targeted text searches because codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this host; no graph results are assumed. Goal: guarded chat uses configured permission posture, avoids blanket shell/edit prompts, and retains explicit escape, sandbox-down, configured ask, command-safety and non-read-only discovered MCP prompts. Binding implementation order: US-001 -> US-002; US-003 is independent; US-004 depends on US-001/002/003; US-005 depends on US-004. All stories are security-sensitive sessions/access control and require three-session-tdd, including the smaller config resolver story.

Verified baseline and impact: packages/nax/src/chat/chat-mode.ts:12 hard-codes guarded to profile ask/bashApproval gated; chatModeOfMeta at :23 maps persisted ask to guarded and must remain unchanged. packages/nax-agent/src/session/native-backend-options.ts:164 nativeProfileRules rejects ask with non-gated approval and returns only bashApproval, allowUnsandboxed and allowUnsandboxedCommands. Keep that validator and its exact return shape unchanged; add a separate native-posture-rules.ts instead of changing ask semantics for other embedders. parseNativeBackendOptions validates a strict schema but preserves the caller-owned raw object (packages/nax-agent/test/unit/session/native-backend-options.test.ts:25). Thus validating sandbox in OptionsSchema is insufficient to deliver default-filled sandbox data: nativePostureRules must obtain the parsed SandboxConfigSchema output, not forward raw partial input. Sandbox schema nested prefaults/defaults are defined in packages/nax-agent/src/config/schemas-sandbox.ts:21 and DEFAULT_SANDBOX_CONFIG derives from parsing {} at :61. Public sandbox option must use z.input<typeof SandboxConfigSchema> so network-only inputs typecheck without manufacturing required output fields.

US-001 agent flow: packages/nax-agent/src/session/native-backend.ts:63 openNative currently resolves profile rules, gets the launcher, resolves providers, builds support and opens NativeSessionAdapter. Add posture resolution alongside profile resolution; pass parsed sandbox to the launcher and parsed ask/deny grants to support. packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-tool-support.ts:179 composes tool grants and ask rules; configured asks must append after profile asks and provider asks, not replace them. resolveSessionLauncher currently uses DEFAULT_SANDBOX_CONFIG; add optional config with its existing default fallback. Deny and ask precedence must remain that of compileToolPolicy. packages/nax-agent/src/tools/policy.ts:313 checks unconditional deny before command handling, while packages/nax-agent/src/tools/policy-command-branch.ts:64 returns through the raw screen before scoped deny/ask evaluation. Preserve that ADR-030 distinction: unconditional Bash/Bash(*) deny holds under raw; scoped Bash patterns are not consulted under raw; non-Bash tool rules continue to apply. No raw screen change is needed.

US-002 runtime flow: packages/nax-agent/src/coding-tools/coding-tool-extras.ts:77 unsandboxedRuntimeOption currently returns only enabled/bashApproval; add alwaysAsk only for the opt-in, retaining absent-key legacy shape. packages/nax-agent/src/tools/runtime-calltool.ts:143 resolveUnsandboxedCall currently uses approval mode alone; widen its option and use alwaysAsk === true || bashApproval !== raw. Existing convertUnsandboxedAllow and resolveAskOutcome already carry the escape reason; do not invent another approval path. packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session-types.ts:47 AgentSessionHostPorts needs the commandShadow port and the strict backend hostPorts schema must check observe/settle/drain without cloning away shadow identity. packages/nax-agent/src/coding-tools/coding-tool-support.ts:167 already accepts commandShadow, :265 forwards it, and :304 builds the runtime unsandboxed option; add askOnUnsandboxed as a plain argument property, with no new conditional in buildCodingToolSupport. packages/nax-agent/src/tools/runtime.ts:233 is the existing single-line unsandboxed option declaration; keep the widened declaration on one line because the file is at its 600-line limit. Existing runtime shadow tap and guard consumers are at runtime.ts:427 and :575. Guard failure remains fail-open through existing resolveGuardDenial; the opt-in only wires it to chat. Preserve non-read-only provider asks when moving guarded to full by adding askDiscoveredTools; profile ask continues asking as before. Effective gated fallback must be used both in runtime support and NativeSessionAdapter.openSession resolvedPermissions, not just one of them. Sandbox kind is captured once at open.

US-003 config: packages/nax/src/config/permissions.ts:182 lookupStageBlock already implements block selection/inherit walk/default fallback; widen only its file-local stage argument to string. It selects a whole block, not a per-field merge. stageRules at :205 and resolvePermissions at :232 remain unchanged. Resolve tui directly from the selected block's ask/deny/bashApproval and reuse resolveBashApproval (packages/nax-agent/src/config/bash-approval.ts:33; defaults to raw via :22). Do not read permissionProfile, allow or allowedTools and do not add tui to PipelineStage or MCP pipeline-stage enums. Export TuiPermissions and resolveTuiPermissions via packages/nax/src/config/index.ts:35-36. No config schema expansion is required: packages/nax/src/config/schemas-execution.ts:215 uses a string-keyed record, :305 uses the shared sandbox schema, and packages/nax/src/config/config-guards.ts:464 validates arbitrary block keys/inheritance. Config loader already invokes validatePermissionsBlock at packages/nax/src/config/loader.ts:224 and :545. Warnings use getSafeLogger warn on stage permissions; collapse multiple raw scoped Bash patterns to one warning per resolution. Escalate resolves to gated with its separate single warning. Do not accidentally classify unconditional Bash/Bash(*) deny as an ignored scoped deny.

US-004 resource opening: packages/nax/src/chat/open-chat-session.ts:88 sessionMeta validates persisted metadata and overrides effective settings; :127 sessionOptions constructs nativeBackend; :164 openChatSession owns the storage lock and session creation/resume. Resolve effective mode from explicit request or validated stored mode before posture policy is selected. Resolve posture once at the resource opener for guarded only, then pass the same value to metadata/options; never reconstruct policy from stored bashApproval. New sessions retain meta.mode ask while using native profile full. Full opens must not resolve posture or log its warnings. Resume and /mode or /model reopen under current config without changing existing metadata persistence sites. SessionOptions must use current settings rather than treating stored policy as authoritative. packages/nax/src/chat/subagent-session.ts:49 has injectable dependencies, :57 constructs options and :168 runSubagent is the opener; resolve there once for guarded and forward posture into the helper. Subagents retain memory transcripts, narrowing, loopHandlerRole subagent and existing cancellation/error lifecycle; no commandShadow/hostPorts. Export chatBackendPosture through packages/nax/src/chat/index.ts:33-34. Direct consumers to preserve are chat-host.ts:253, :340 and :377 (open/resume/switch), subagent-runs.ts:175 (nested opens), and existing mode/meta helpers.

US-005 lifecycle: packages/nax-agent/src/command-safety/build.ts:36 buildCommandShadow already returns undefined without config.shadow, derives command-safety directory under outputDir, and uses env for auth. Reuse it through _openChatSessionDeps; do not reuse the run-scoped buildDispatchAskWiring or its approvals-cache side effects (packages/nax/src/interaction/dispatch-ask.ts:112). Guarded main opens use request.storage.dir and meta.sessionId, including resume, and env from deps. Omit hostPorts entirely when no shadow exists. Returned release drains before lock release; both backend synchronous throw and create/resume rejection after shadow creation must drain and release before preserving the same original error. Existing CommandShadow contract is total (packages/nax-agent/src/command-safety/types.ts:92), with its bounded timeout behavior reused. Rows belong to <sessionsDir>/command-safety/<sessionId>.jsonl; metadata suffix is .session.json in packages/nax-agent/src/session-store/storage.ts:33. packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/chat-builder.ts:17 is the shared permission sentence; agents-builder.ts imports and uses it for subagents, so change the shared sentence without unrelated TUI copy changes.

Tests and implementation seams: agent unit tests already cover strict backend validation and raw object identity (native-backend-options.test.ts), profile ask behavior and full's gated-only Bash asks (session-tool-support.test.ts:98-117), unsandboxed runtime shape (coding-tool-extras.test.ts), and escape routing (runtime-unsandboxed.test.ts). Create only the three new files assigned to US-001 and one new integration-style unit test file for US-002. Session-level behavior tests use the scripted-provider/session readers in packages/nax-agent/test/helpers/agent-session.ts and stubSessionSandboxDeps in test/helpers/session-sandbox-deps.ts:108; these avoid real model/network/sandbox availability. Important helper hazard: agent-session.ts:173 sessionOptions explicitly destructures and forwards native-only options; extend its forwarding if tests use it, otherwise new options silently disappear. Restore all _deps changes with shared helpers. Regressions must fail against old code before counting. outOfScope: Full mode does not read `execution.permissions.tui` or `execution.commandSafety` and never asks; its only change is that its sandbox is built from `execution.sandbox`.
`allow` and legacy `allowedTools` lists in `execution.permissions.tui` are not read: chat's `full` profile already grants every tool, so an allow list cannot widen anything.

A `tui` block replaces the `default` block as a whole (existing block-lookup semantics): a `tui` block that sets only `bashApproval` does not inherit `default`'s `ask` or `deny` lists unless it names `inherit: "default"`.

Under a resolved `bashApproval` of `raw`, pattern-scoped `Bash(...)` ask and deny rules are not consulted (ADR-030 raw pass-through, as in `nax run`); this feature does not change the raw Bash screen.

`GitCommit` is not offered in chat sessions (it is declared only when the protected-paths policy carries git ignore patterns, which chat does not set), so a `GitCommit` ask rule matches nothing in chat; commits made through `Bash` follow the Bash posture.

`Mcp(...)` rules in `execution.permissions.tui` are not expanded into concrete MCP tool rules for chat; the MCP asks in guarded chat are the non-read-only discovered-tool asks carried by `askDiscoveredTools`.

The sandbox state is decided once when a session opens; a sandbox that becomes unavailable mid-session does not switch that session to asking until it is reopened (resume, `/mode` or `/model` switch).

Subagent sessions do not receive a command shadow or the commandSafety guard; the subagent's own posture (bash mode, ask/deny rules, escape, sandbox-down and discovered-tool asks, sandbox config) is wired.
The nax-agent `ask` profile, `askRulesFor`, `nativeProfileRules` and its return shape keep their behaviour; no embedder's options change meaning.
The ACP server (`packages/nax-agent-acp`) session options are not changed.
No TUI wording changes besides the instruction paragraph: the footer label, the `/mode` picker text (`asks before risky actions`) and `/mode` behaviour are unchanged.
No migration of stored session metadata: a stored `bashApproval` is overwritten in memory at open and written only where it is written today.
